note_tweet.text:
Who Verifies the Verifier? Co-Evolving Inspectable Graders with Self-Improving Agents
https://t.co/TlF7PmewFs
✍️ Xing Zhang, Guanghui Wang et al. via @arxiv 

👉 The authors introduce "Double Ratchet", a framework that addresses the issue of reward hacking in self-improving AI loops by co-evolving an inspectable verifier alongside the agent. 

👉 Rather than relying on rigid rubrics or biased LLM judges, this evolving grader builds small, deterministic detectors synthesized from clustered failures and scales them against anchored reference sets to reliably score code, SQL, and text generation tasks.

💡 By shifting the focus of RSI from the agent's output to the verifier's own code, the researchers deliver a brilliant architectural countermeasure to the silent threat of AI optimisation echo chambers. 

💡 This mechanism proves that the safest path to autonomous machine reasoning is not to build a more dominant judge, but to construct a dynamic, highly transparent system of checks and balances where grading criteria evolve in tandem with the skills being evaluated.

CFR is pleased to announce a transformative $15 million gift from the Blavatnik Family Foundation to strengthen and expand the Blavatnik Internship Program. Including both endowment and current-use support, this generous commitment more than doubles the foundation’s original investment in the program and builds on its remarkable success.

“We hope this expanded program will open doors for the next generation of leaders and equip them to tackle the defining challenges of our time,” said Len Blavatnik, founder of Access Industries and CFR life member.

This new gift allows CFR to grow its program by offering full-time internships for the summer cohort and to meet growing operating costs. The expansion will give participants a richer, more sustained experience at the institution, deepening their engagement with CFR’s scholars and programs. The Blavatnik Internship Program reflects CFR’s commitment to cultivating diverse, talented voices in the foreign policy community and preparing tomorrow’s global experts to navigate an increasingly complex world.

“This gift expands access to paid internships, ensuring that talented students and recent graduates can pursue opportunities regardless of financial circumstances. It strengthens one of the most competitive and prestigious internship programs in the field and ensures that CFR remains a place where tomorrow’s leaders come to learn, engage, and prepare for careers in service to the nation and the world. We are deeply grateful to Len Blavatnik and the Blavatnik Family Foundation for their extraordinary generosity, vision, and long-standing partnership with CFR," said CFR President @MikeFroman. 

Read more: https://t.co/eK8rD37zyQ
